limits: Both browser pages are frozen while the owned allocator approaches the cgroup reserve, then resumed after release and the actual retry backoff.
These cases cover idle-service process-tree removal and independent source restoration; they do not establish in-flight request/command behavior under sustained pressure.
The pressure cgroup peak includes the artificial allocator and is not the application footprint. allocated_bytes is cumulative allocation per allocator instance, including its released observation.
PID samples establish observed process-tree removal/replacement, not a separate PID-reuse authority proof.
Local uses OPFS/native correspondence. Complete native/WASM retained memory, other servers/devices and hard memory bounds remain open.

limits: Whole final app image, including Spin, bridge and language servers, under asserted 2 CPU / 2 GiB limits.
Local browser uses OPFS/native marker correspondence; no physical permissions measured.
Browser requests run through actual installed plugin, authorization and native LSP transports.
UI latency includes WebDriver polling; no speed improvement inferred from cold/warm samples.
RSS includes allocator retention; post-GC CDP JS heap excludes complete WASM/browser memory.
Engine process readings sample every second and at query boundaries; short peaks can be missed. Cgroup peak includes bounded control reads.
Local-stage RSS includes any still-idle Remote server in this shared bridge.
Each workload has one first-load sample per mode; repeated-run p95 is descriptive, not SLO confidence.
PID observations describe process continuity and changes; they do not assign a response to one process during overlap.
Browser and proof-mirror clients run outside the server cgroup; workspace/state use owned host bind mounts.
